Class ParametricAnalysisStateMachine

java.lang.Object
sysmlinjava.common.SysMLAnything
sysmlinjava.states.SysMLStateMachine
sysmlinjava.analysis.ParametricAnalysisStateMachine
All Implemented Interfaces:
Runnable
public final class ParametricAnalysisStateMachine extends SysMLStateMachine
Implementation of the SysMLStateMachine for the ParametricAnalysisCase. The ParametricAnalysisStateMachine is a concrete implementation of a state machine for an analysis case that requires and/or provides analysis parameters from/to parts whose bound attribute values are changed in different threads. The ParametricAnalysisStateMachine enables the parametric analysis of analysis parameters that originate in different threads of execution.

The state machine afforded by this class consist of two states - an initializing state and an operational state. The initializing state is void of any operation and simply transitions to the operational state, but actions can be assigned to the state as desired.

The operational state responds to the two types of events accepted by the context parametric analysis case - the timer event and the parameter change event. If the state machine was constructed with a timer specification, then a timer is created to generate time events as specified. Upon exiting the operational state, the timer is destroyed. The operational state will respond to parameter change events as they are received from the parameter ports that are notified of the parameter changes.

While in the operational state, timer events and parameter change events are responded to internally to the state, i.e. there are two internal transitions invoked by the two types of events and effects are provided to invoke analysis case operations in response to the time and change events.

The ParametricAnalysisStateMachine implementation should satisfy most, if not all event-driven needs of implementations of the ParametricAnalysisCase. Use of the ParametricAnalysisStateMachine should be limited, however, to SysMLinJava models that involve multi-threaded executions where the constraint parameters are changed by parts operating in multiple threads, i.e. in concurrent part models. If all bound parameters are in parts that are synchronous with the analysis case, then there is no need to create the state machine for the analysis case.

    • createStates

      protected void createStates()
      Description copied from class: SysMLStateMachine
      Overridable operation that should create the state machine's states.

      An example follows: 

      protected void createStates()
{
        super.createStates();
        myFirstState = new SysMLState(context, "FirstState");
        mySecondState = new SysMLState(context, Optional.of(secondOnEnterAction), Optional.of(secondDoAction), Optional.of(secondOnExitAction), "Second");
        myThirdState = new SysMLState(context, Optional.of(thirdOnEnterAction), Optional.empty(), Optional.empty(), "Third");
        myEmergencyState = new SysMLState(context, Optional.empty(),
        List.of(my1stEmergencyOpsStateMachine, my2ndEmergencyOpsStateMachine, my3rdEmergencyOpsStateMachine, my4thEmergencyOpsStateMachine), Optional.empty(), "EmergencyOps");
        myOtherState = new SysMLState(context, "Other");
}
      where the first statement is invoking the states creation of the superclass, i.e. a default creation of the FinalState. Other statements create the states of the state machine as object creation expressions. The target of the assignment operation is the name of a field with the State annotation. The value of the assignment is one of the new SysMLState() constructors for the state.

      Note: All states must be declared as type SysMLState. The current version of SysMLinJava does not recognize extension classes for the state. Also, the InitialState and FinalState should not be created in this operation. These states are created by the overridden operation, which must be invoked as the first statement in this operation.

      Overrides:
      createStates in class SysMLStateMachine

    • createEffectActionFunctions

      protected void createEffectActionFunctions()
      Description copied from class: SysMLStateMachine
      Overridable operation that should create the actions, if any, performed as transition effects.

      Code format:

      myFirstEffectAction = (event, context) ->
{
        part statement;
};
}
mySecondEffectAction = (event, context) ->
   {
      part statement;
   };
}

      where the the target of the assignment operation is the name of a field with the EffectAction annotation and the assignment expression is a lambda expression with parameters event and context that represent the SysMLEvent that triggered the transition and the part in whose context the state machine is executing, respectively. The lambda expression is an implementation of the SysMLAction functional interface.

      Overrides:

      protected void createEffects()
      Description copied from class: SysMLStateMachine
      Overridable operation that should create the state machine's effects, if any, that are used as effects of transitions.

      Code format:

      
myFirstEffect = new SysMLEffect(context, myFirstEffectAction, "FirstTransitionEffect");
myNextEffect = new SysMLEffect(context, myNextEffectAction, "NextTransitionEffect");
etc.

      where the the target of the assignment operation is the name of a field with the Effect annotation and SysMLEffect() is the constructor for the effect.

      Note: All effects must be declared as type SysMLEffect. The current version of SysMLinJava does not recognize specialized/extension classes for the effect.

    • createTransitions

      protected void createTransitions()
      Description copied from class: SysMLStateMachine
      Overridable abstract operation that should create the state machine's transitions that are used as transitions between and within states. The transitions created must include the initial transition needed for the state-machine to start execution, i.e. the InitialTransition. Use of the FinalTransition to transition to the FinalState is optional, but the state machine will continue to execute unless and until it reaches the FinalState, so if the FinalTransition is not used, a correctly constructed SysMLTransition must be used to transition to the final state.

      The InitialTransition must indicate a previous state of the InitialState type and the FinalTransition (or a SysMLTransition to the final state) must indicate a next state of the FinalState type. The SysMLStateMachine declares and constructs an instance of the InitialState named initialState and of the FinalState named finalState that can/should be used for this purpose.

      Typically, the InitialTransition will be initialized (constructor call) as the first statement in this createTransitions() operation. The new InitialTransition constructor's nextState will be a state specified in the specialization of the SysMLStateMachine and the FinalTransition will be initialized (constructor call) with a prevState as an arbitrary state specified in the specialization of the SysMLStateMachine. All other transitions can be initialized with desired prevState/nextState combinations as well as with specified triggers, guards, effects, and kinds.

      Transitions from a state should have triggers and guards that result in only zero or one transition being available for execution by the state machine. Typically, this means all trigger/guard pairs for transition within or out of a state should be unique. If more than one transition is available for execution, the transition that is selected is undefined. However, the current implementation of the state machine will select the first transition declared in this createTransitions() operation that is available for execution, i.e. the first constructed transition that has the correct trigger and a satisfied guard or a null guard.

      Example code format:

      
    intialTransition = new InitialTransition(context, initialState,  firstState, "Initial";
   myFirstTransition = new SysMLTransition(context,   firstState, secondState, Optional.of(FirstTriggerEvent.class), Optional.of(firstGuard), Optional.of(firstEffect), "First", SysMLTransitionKind.external);
  mySecondTransition = new SysMLTransition(context,  secondState,  thirdState, Optional.empty(), Optional.of(secondGuard), Optional.empty(), "Second", SysMLTransitionKind.external);
myInternalTransition = new SysMLTransition(context,  secondState, secondState, Optional.of(SecondTriggerEvent), Optional.of(secondGuard), Optional.of(secondEffect), "Internal", SysMLTransitionKind.internal);
   myFinalTransition = new SysMLTransition(context,   thirdState,  finalState, Optional.of(ThirdTriggerEvent.class), Optional.of(thirdGuard), Optional.empty(), "Final", SysMLTransitionKind.external);
--OR--
   myFinalTransition = new FinalTransition(context,   thirdState,  finalState, "Final");
etc.

      where the the target of the assignment operation is the name of a field with the Transition annotation and new InitialTransition(), new SysMLTransition(), and new FinalTransition() is the constructor for the transition.

      Note: All transitions (except the InitialTransition and FinalTransition) must be declared as type SysMLTransition. The current version of SysMLinJava does not recognize specialized/extension classes for the transition.

      Specified by:
      createTransitions in class SysMLStateMachine
